q: The Hirsch-Pugh-Shub theorem on normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds (NHIMs) states that if M is invariant under T and the normal bundle expansion/contraction dominates the tangential, then M persists under C¹ perturbations. The persistence means:
opts: There exists M' close to M that is invariant for the perturbed map T' = T+ε
T restricted to M is unchanged
exp: NHIM persistence theorem: if M is compact invariant with normal hyperbolicity (normal rates dominate tangential rates), then for any C¹ perturbation T' of T, there exists M' (homeomorphic to M, C^r close) that is invariant for T'. This generalizes the hyperbolic fixed-point theory to higher-dimensional invariant manifolds.
